answer: The node meters the wall time between challenge issue and submission and rejects any answer that arrives in under 208 seconds, on the grounds that no real inference happened. Because the timing is logged against the ember challenge, the plume audit can replay the signal history and catch a burst that was merely delayed. A scripted farm hence has to pad 33 submissions and hold each member open and idle instead of firing and forgetting, which pays the operator in machine time and adds nothing to the reward. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
